beats.label: S1 · Fired and discarded
beats.text: Already divorced after Mel's affair with his best friend Nick, hedge fund manager Coop is fired by his boss Jack via a fabricated HR complaint.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The double loss of career and marriage is the pressure that pushes Coop into crime — everything else follows from it.

beats.label: S1 · First theft
beats.text: To keep his family's lifestyle afloat without a paycheck, Coop pockets cash at a neighbor's party, then returns the next day to burgle the empty house.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The pattern the whole series is built on: robbing his own social circle to sustain the appearance of belonging to it.

beats.label: S1 · Elena and Lu
beats.text: Nick's housekeeper Elena catches Coop mid-robbery and proposes they team up, using her network of maids for intel and Lu as their pawnshop fence.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the crew — Elena, Lu, Coop — that runs the operation from here on.

beats.label: S1 · Sam and Paul
beats.text: Coop's on-off affair with neighbor Sam sours after a bad art-heist night with dealer Christian, and Coop later finds Sam's ex-husband Paul dead in her house.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Coop's entanglement with Sam and his presence at Paul's death are the ingredients Sam will use to frame him.

beats.label: S1 · Arrested at the funeral
beats.text: Detective Lin finds bloody evidence and the murder weapon in Coop's car and arrests him at Paul's funeral, in front of the entire neighborhood.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The public collapse of Coop's life — job gone, marriage gone, now branded a killer in front of everyone he knows.

beats.label: S1 · Sam framed him
beats.text: Coop and Elena find a hidden suicide note proving Sam staged Paul's death to keep his $20M life insurance; Sam is arrested and Coop is cleared.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The reversal that removes Sam from the board and returns Coop to Westmont as a wronged man.

beats.label: S1 · Chooses the thief's life
beats.text: Offered his old job back by Jack, Coop instead steals a painting from Jack's mansion, choosing the thief's life over the finance world that discarded him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The show's declaration of what Coop actually is now. The next season starts from this choice.

cliffhanger.text: Coop has beaten a murder charge and been welcomed back into Westmont — but instead of returning to Jack's firm he's stolen from him and doubled down on the burglaries. Everyone he loves believes he is innocent of everything.
questions: How long can Coop keep the thefts hidden from Mel, his kids, and Barney?
Where does the escalation end when he's willing to rob his old boss?
Is Sam finished, or will she come back at him from prison?

characters.name: Andrew "Coop" Cooper
characters.line: Fired hedge fund manager turned career burglar; just beat a murder charge and chose the thief's life over returning to finance.

characters.name: Mel Cooper
characters.line: Coop's therapist ex-wife; ended her affair with Nick, defended Coop through the trial, and still loves him.

characters.name: Sam Levitt
characters.line: The neighbor Coop was sleeping with, now jailed for framing him for the staged 'murder' of her ex-husband Paul to collect a $20M life insurance payout.

characters.name: Nick
characters.line: Coop's best friend and former NBA champion; Mel's ex-affair partner who has accepted she still loves Coop.

characters.name: Elena
characters.line: Nick's housekeeper turned Coop's full partner in the crew; runs intel through her housekeeper network and drove the getaway car all season.

characters.name: Lu
characters.line: Bronx pawnshop owner and the fence for every piece Coop and Elena steal; a hard, dangerous business partner.

characters.name: Jack Bailey
characters.line: Coop's former boss who engineered his firing to absorb his accounts; unaware Coop just stole a painting from his mansion.

characters.name: Barney Choi
characters.line: Coop's business manager and closest friend outside Westmont; still doesn't know Coop is a thief.

beats.label: S2 · Barney learns and joins
beats.text: A back spasm mid-heist forces Coop to call Barney for help, exposing the burglaries; Barney signs on and launders the cash through Nick's gym franchise.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Pulls Barney and Nick's business into the crime — the structure that unravels at the season's end.

beats.label: S2 · Ashe arrives
beats.text: Shipping billionaire Owen Ashe buys a mansion from the ostracized Sam and pursues her, then catches Coop on hidden camera stealing a rare Wharton book from his home.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's antagonist and the leverage he'll use against Coop.

beats.label: S2 · Blackmailed into Excelsior
beats.text: Ashe — sanctioned as a suspected arms dealer — blackmails Coop with the tape into funneling $400M into Jack Bailey's exclusive Excelsior fund on his behalf.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The engine of the season: Coop is now working for the man who has him on tape.

beats.label: S2 · Greece, then Ron
beats.text: Coop lands the Excelsior investment on a trip to Greece with Jack, then returns home to find his estranged father Ron has died and meets Ron's secret longtime lover.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Cements the trap and shifts the family — Coop is grieving while Ashe tightens the screws.

beats.label: S2 · The squeeze
beats.text: Ashe's lawyer DeMille freezes the cash laundered through Nick's gyms and Ashe demands more investment, tightening his grip on Coop, Barney, and Nick.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The financial choke that makes the confrontation with Ashe inevitable.

beats.label: S2 · Ashe dies in the cover-up
beats.text: Confronted over the returned investment, a drugged Ashe catches fire and rampages with a gun; Coop, Barney, and Nick then cover up his accidental death by drowning.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's climax and the shared secret that binds the three men into next season.

beats.label: S2 · The evidence and the book
beats.text: Weeks later DeMille quietly hands Coop the blackmail tape — Mel witnesses the handoff — and Ashe's sunken car is finally discovered as Mel writes a book about Coop.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets three ticking clocks for next season: Mel's suspicion, the police finding Ashe, and Mel's book about him.

cliffhanger.text: Ashe is at the bottom of a lake but his car has just surfaced, and Mel has seen DeMille handing Coop something. Nick has fired Barney and blown up his marriage; Elena has cleared her debts by letting a drug dealer rob Nick's mansion; Coop's inner circle is fracturing on every side.
questions: How much of the handoff did Mel piece together, and what goes into her book?
Will the recovered car lead police to Coop, Barney, or Nick?
Who really orchestrated Coop's kidnapping — Cricket Birch, or someone else still watching him?

characters.name: Andrew "Coop" Cooper
characters.line: Now an established burglar with a New York office; covered up the death of the arms dealer who was blackmailing him and just got the tape back.

characters.name: Mel Cooper
characters.line: Reconciled emotionally with Coop and rewriting her book around his ordeals; just witnessed DeMille handing him something she doesn't understand.

characters.name: Sam Levitt
characters.line: Rehabilitated in Westmont after community service and a brief romance with Ashe; ended it before helping cover up his death and reconciled with Mel.

characters.name: Nick
characters.line: Fronted the gym franchise that laundered the crew's cash; drove the car that killed Ashe, is drowning in guilt, and has just fired Barney.

characters.name: Elena
characters.line: Newly a US citizen; distanced from Coop after his silence and settled her family's debt by letting the dealer Félix rob Nick's mansion.

characters.name: Barney Choi
characters.line: Coop's business manager and now a knowing partner in the crimes; fired by Nick and separated from his pregnant wife Grace.

characters.name: Owen Ashe
characters.line: Sanctioned shipping billionaire and suspected arms dealer who blackmailed Coop; presumed drowned after the cover-up, his car now recovered from the lake.

characters.name: Jack Bailey
characters.line: Coop's former boss and Excelsior fund manager; accepted the return of Ashe's investment once Coop warned him of its illegality.
